text.p: These are the highlights of the main Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro newspapers this morning.
GAZETA MERCANTIL
-- BRAZILIAN EXPORTS WORRY ARGENTINA
The growth in Brazilian exports to Argentina, which in August practically closed a bilateral trade gap that has persisted for two years, is beginning to worry the Buenos Aires government.
-- FOR FINANCE MINISTER, TALK OF RECESSION IS "BULLSHIT"

Slamming the idea that Brazil may let up in the fight on inflation to spur faster growth, Finance Minister Pedro Malan said "this story of recession in Brazil is garbage, bullshit." Malan, speaking in Washington at the U.S.-Brazilian Chamber of Commerce, said the word was not translatable to Portuguese.
-- GOVERNMENT PLANS TO REVIEW PENSION RULES

A revision of the formula used to calculate public and private pensions and cuts in expenses that should shrink public spending by two to 2.5 billion reais will be announced by the government by year's end.
O GLOBO
-- CENTRAL BANK PROBES SAO PAULO MAYORAL CANDIDATE FOR FRAUD

The Central Bank yesterday admitted it is investigating possible fraud in the purchase of Sao Paulo municipal treasury notes while Celso Pitta, the front-running candidate in the race for Sao Paulo mayor, was city finance secretary.
-- RE-ELECTION MOBILIZES ECONOMIC TEAM

The Brazilian government's economic team has taken to politicking in the last few days, campaigning on behalf of a constitutional amendment to allow President Fernando Henrique Cardoso to stand for re-election.
-- SWISS MAN SUSPECTED IN CHILD PROSTITUTION RING

A 46-year-old Swiss man suspected of belonging to an international child prostitution ring turned himself in to authorities for questioning. He is being investigated for allegedly arranging meetings between tourists and Brazilian children.
FOLHA DE SAO PAULO
-- GOVERNMENT WANTS TO TAKE LAND FROM DEBTORS
The Brazilian government wants to seize unproductive land from landowners who fail to pay the Rural Territorial Tax and turn the property over to the state's agrarian reform program.
-- BRAZIL MINISTER SAYS SAO PAULO MAYOR "ROBBED" MAYORALTY
Brazilian Communications Minister Sergio Motta accused Sao Paulo Mayor Paulo Maluf of "robbing" the mayoralty by overpricing city projects. Maluf had no comment.
-- ISRAEL MEETING BEGINS UNDER THREAT
Egypt's absence could doom today's meeting in Washington to resolve the current crisis between Israelis and Palestinians.
Reuters has not verified the stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
-- James Craig, Sao Paulo newsroom 5511 232 4411
